rules.title: Santa Ana ban on algorithmic rent-setting software
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use, and vendors may not sell, license or provide, algorithmic rent-setting software that uses nonpublic competitor data for residential rental property in Santa Ana. Affected tenants can sue for injunctive relief, damages, or civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation plus attorney's fees.
rules.key_value: ban on algorithmic devices using nonpublic competitor data; civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation
rules.quoted_span: prohibits the sale, licensing, provision and use of certain algorithmic rent-setting software for residential rental properties.
rules.effective_date_note: Article reports first reading Feb. 17, 2026 and final vote set for March 3, 2026; the effective date is not stated, and final adoption is not confirmed in this document.
rules.penalty: Injunctive relief, damages, or civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation, plus attorney's fees
rules.exemptions: Pricing software relying solely on publicly available data, aggregate historical data, or tools used to comply with affordable housing program requirements
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental property within Santa Ana city limits
rules.conflict_note: Document is a news item describing first reading only; adoption and effective date not confirmed here. Ordinance number is not stated in the document.

unverifiable_exemptions: tools used to comply with affordable housing program requirements

parsed.doc_summary: News article on Santa Ana's ordinance banning algorithmic rent-setting software (first reading Feb. 17, 2026, final vote set for Mar. 3, 2026). It describes the prohibition, exemptions and a tenant private right of action with penalties up to $1,000 per violation. It also mentions the city's existing rent stabilization ordinance but gives no operative details.
